events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
At 14:17 the rider sent a message naming a specific place and purpose — "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes." — and the driver answered "Sure" one minute before the segment began at 14:21 [F9][F10][F4]. That is a rider-named stop agreed before the segment, so under RD-3(a) the segment driven to reach the named place is not a detour and its extra kilometres are exempt in full [RD-3]. The car did stop at the place the rider named, standing 4 min 0 s at 14:23–14:27, which matches the 3–4 minutes the rider offered [F2][F9].

The trace fixes the required finding: F4 is grounded rider_named_stop and the finding that follows is exempt. The stationary fact F2 sits inside the 14:21–14:31 segment, and the driver's statement — that he drove to Clementi Mall and waited — places the segment at the place the rider named, not somewhere else [F12][F2]. RD-3(a) does not reduce the exemption for the length of the stop or the distance of the named place, so the whole way there, including the stationary stretch, is exempt; it would be wrong to carve the loop into "the stop" and "the way there" [RD-3].

Nothing else excuses or re-charges that segment. No incident was recorded on the replaced optimal stretch during the trip window, so RD-4(a) does not apply, and the two speed-band readings (band 4 on Ayer Rajah Expressway, band 3 on Jurong Town Hall Road) are neither on the replaced stretch nor exempt on their own under RD-4(b) [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].
